findings.where: Home page · second CTA button (mobile + desktop)
findings.what: CTA says 'Ver el ranking del Mundial' but Mundial was removed from the product. The link correctly points to /penca/libertadores-2026 but the visible label is stale and undermines trust in 5 seconds. The flow spec calls for 'Ver Libertadores'.
findings.fix_hint: Grep the codebase for 'Ver el ranking del Mundial' or 'ranking del Mundial' — likely in the home template (mantia-home shortcode / template-home.php). Change to 'Ver Libertadores' or 'Ver el ranking · Libertadores 2026'.

findings.where: Themed 404 page · primary recovery CTA (3 paths: /penca/no-existe/, /penca/g/bogus/, /penca/me/share/bogus/)
findings.what: Every themed 404 page surfaces a pink primary CTA 'Ver Mundial 2026' linking to /penca/libertadores-2026. Same stale 'Mundial' string. Worse here than the home because the 404 is the moment we recover the visitor — handing them an out-of-date competition reference is high-friction.
findings.fix_hint: In the themed 404 template (probably class-mantia-404.php or a not-found template part), change 'Ver Mundial 2026' to 'Ver Libertadores 2026'. Same source line likely powers all 3 paths.
findings.evidence: /var/folders/9s/r8f3kc7x0vl0v8tddcz010r00000gn/T/qa-lurker-web/08-404-no-existe-mobile.png · accessibility snapshot uid=7_7 / uid=8_7 / uid=9_7 all read 'Ver Mundial 2026'

findings.where: Share-poster page (/penca/me/share/<token>/) · 'Mandar por WhatsApp' button + card footer
findings.what: The share-poster's 'Mandar por WhatsApp' wa.me href is 'https://wa.me/?text=mantia3.wpcomstaging.com%2F' — just the root domain, no specific path. The card footer also shows only 'mantia3.wpcomstaging.com/'. Recipients of the share won't know what's being shared until they click. Defeats the recipient-friendly intent of the share-poster.
findings.fix_hint: Include the sharer's /penca/me/<edit_token>/ or /penca/g/<group_view_token>/ in the wa.me text body and in the card footer. Look in template-share.php / class-mantia-share for the wa.me URL builder.

findings.what: All Mantia CPTs have show_in_rest enabled and are publicly listable by anonymous users. /wp-json/wp/v2/mantia_prediction exposes 10 prediction records titled with player display name + match score (e.g. 'Florencia QA Returning: River Plate 0-1 Boca Juniors'). Anyone can scrape who-predicted-what without ever needing a view_token. View_tokens themselves do NOT leak in meta (private meta is gated), but the listing alone is a privacy paper-cut — predictions are meant to be private until /me/ reveal.
findings.fix_hint: Set show_in_rest=false on mantia_prediction, mantia_user, mantia_group, mantia_match CPT registrations, OR add a rest_authentication filter that returns empty for unauthenticated callers. Predictions and player names should never be enumerable anonymously.
findings.evidence: /wp-json/wp/v2/mantia_prediction returns 200 with 10 entries. Sample title: 'Florencia QA Returning: River Plate 0-1 Boca Juniors'. /wp-json/wp/v2/mantia_user returns 6 player names ('Florencia QA Returning' etc). /wp-json/wp/v2/mantia_group returns 7 group titles ('Los Pibes del 92', 'Pibes del 5', 'Penca del Barrio'...).

findings.what: Both /service-worker.js and /manifest.json return nginx 404 at canonical paths. They only work at /service-worker.js/ and /manifest.json/ (trailing slash). The page itself registers '/service-worker.js/' so PWA actually works, but anything probing canonical paths (PWA Builder, Lighthouse, third-party crawlers, social previews) will mark Mantia as broken.
findings.fix_hint: Add rewrite rules so canonical paths (no trailing slash) resolve. Either via .htaccess or via the rewrite rule that produces the trailing-slash version — drop the trailing slash, or add an additional rewrite for the non-slash variant.
findings.evidence: fetch('/service-worker.js') → 404 nginx HTML; fetch('/service-worker.js/') → 200 application/javascript, 2612 bytes starting 'Mantia · Service Worker'. fetch('/manifest.json') → 200 (this one works without slash). Page DOM: `register('\/service-worker.js\/')`.

findings.what: Subtitle reads 'mar 19 may – jue 21 may · 8 partidos' using en-dash '–'. The flow spec expects arrow '→' between dates. Visually, '–' between two day-abbrevs is harder to scan than '→'. Polish-only — both are valid Spanish typography.
findings.fix_hint: If the flow spec is the source of truth, replace en-dash with U+2192 RIGHTWARDS ARROW in the competition-page template's date range builder.

findings.what: When the bad slug is a competition (/penca/<slug>), the H1 is descriptive: 'Competencia "no-existe" no encontrada'. For /penca/g/<bad-token> and /penca/me/share/<bad-token> the H1 is the friendlier 'Este link de penca no funciona o ya venció.' The competition-not-found message echoing the literal slug back to the user feels technical and could be reflected XSS bait — the slug is HTML-escaped in title text but still feels off-tone vs the friendlier sibling.
findings.fix_hint: Unify both 404 messages to the friendlier 'Este link no funciona o ya venció.' regardless of /penca/* subpath. Skip echoing the user-supplied slug.

findings.what: Critical primetime check passes: NO Lorem-ipsum / Assembler fallthrough on any /penca/* path. All three return HTTP 404 with the themed Mantia design (cancha green, Archivo Black, ear-pill back arrow, recovery CTAs). The hard-routed themed 404 is well-engineered.

findings.what: Competition pages are clean and correct: exactly 2 pills (Libertadores 2026 + Libertadores semanal — no Mundial, no Sudamericana, no LigaUY, no 'Esta semana' orphans). Phase header hoists per day ('MAR 19 MAY · FASE DE GRUPOS · FECHA 5'). Fecha 5 vs Fecha 6 hoisted correctly on the parent. Team and country names all in Spanish (São Paulo, Vélez Sársfield, Universidad Católica, Atlético Bucaramanga). Empty ranking state 'Todavía no hay puntos cargados.' renders gracefully.

findings.where: Home page and competition page initial paint
findings.what: Performance is excellent. Home + competition pages: DOMContentLoaded ~740ms, transferSize ~48KB. No render-blocking external CSS bundles, fonts inlined, QR code lazy via 3rd-party API but doesn't block paint. Well under the <500ms budget for everything-but-network.

Install banner correctly appears on mobile (390px wide, viewport <768) with friendly Spanish copy 'Agregalo a tu pantalla de inicio para abrirlo en un toque. · Instalar · ✕'. Hidden on desktop (1280px). Dismissal persists via localStorage key 'mantia-pwa-dismissed' so it doesn't nag repeat visitors. Polished UX.
